paragraphs.text: At that season Jesus went on the sabbath day through the grainfields; and his disciples were hungry and began to pluck ears and to eat.
paragraphs.original: Ἐν ἐκείνῳ τῷ καιρῷ ἐπορεύθη ὁ Ἰησοῦς τοῖς σάββασιν διὰ τῶν σπορίμων· οἱ δὲ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ ἐπείνασαν καὶ ἤρξαντο τίλλειν στάχυας καὶ ἐσθίειν.
paragraphs.translit: En ekeinō tō kairō eporeuthē ho Iēsous tois sabbasin dia tōn sporimōn· hoi de mathētai autou epeinasan kai ērxanto tillein stachyas kai esthiein.

paragraphs.text: But the Pharisees, when they saw it, said unto him, Behold, thy disciples do that which it is not lawful to do upon the sabbath.
paragraphs.original: οἱ δὲ Φαρισαῖοι ἰδόντες εἶπαν αὐτῷ· Ἰδοὺ οἱ μαθηταί σου ποιοῦσιν ὃ οὐκ ἔξεστιν ποιεῖν ἐν σαββάτῳ.
paragraphs.translit: hoi de Pharisaioi idontes eipan autō· Idou hoi mathētai sou poiousin ho ouk exestin poiein en sabbatō.

paragraphs.text: But he said unto them, Have ye not read what David did, when he was hungry, and they that were with him;
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Οὐκ ἀνέγνωτε τί ἐποίησεν Δαυὶδ ὅτε ἐπείνασεν καὶ οἱ μετʼ αὐτοῦ;
paragraphs.translit: ho de eipen autois· Ouk anegnōte ti epoiēsen Dauid hote epeinasen kai hoi metʼ autou;

paragraphs.text: how he entered into the house of God, and ate the showbread, which it was not lawful for him to eat, neither for them that were with him, but only for the priests?
paragraphs.original: πῶς εἰσῆλθεν εἰς τὸν οἶκον τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ τοὺς ἄρτους τῆς προθέσεως ἔφαγον, ὃ οὐκ ἐξὸν ἦν αὐτῷ φαγεῖν οὐδὲ τοῖς μετʼ αὐτοῦ, εἰ μὴ τοῖς ἱερεῦσιν μόνοις;
paragraphs.translit: pōs eisēlthen eis ton oikon tou theou kai tous artous tēs protheseōs ephagon, ho ouk exon ēn autō phagein oude tois metʼ autou, ei mē tois hiereusin monois;

paragraphs.text: Or have ye not read in the law, that on the sabbath day the priests in the temple profane the sabbath, and are guiltless?
paragraphs.original: ἢ οὐκ ἀνέγνωτε ἐν τῷ νόμῳ ὅτι τοῖς σάββασιν οἱ ἱερεῖς ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ τὸ σάββατον βεβηλοῦσιν καὶ ἀναίτιοί εἰσιν;
paragraphs.translit: ē ouk anegnōte en tō nomō hoti tois sabbasin hoi hiereis en tō hierō to sabbaton bebēlousin kai anaitioi eisin;

paragraphs.text: But I say unto you, that one greater than the temple is here.
paragraphs.original: λέγω δὲ ὑμῖν ὅτι τοῦ ἱεροῦ μεῖζόν ἐστιν ὧδε.
paragraphs.translit: legō de hymin hoti tou hierou meizon estin hōde.

paragraphs.text: But if ye had known what this meaneth, I desire mercy, and not sacrifice, ye would not have condemned the guiltless.
paragraphs.original: εἰ δὲ ἐγνώκειτε τί ἐστιν· Ἔλεος θέλω καὶ οὐ θυσίαν, οὐκ ἂν κατεδικάσατε τοὺς ἀναιτίους.
paragraphs.translit: ei de egnōkeite ti estin· Eleos thelō kai ou thysian, ouk an katedikasate tous anaitious.

paragraphs.text: For the Son of man is lord of the sabbath.
paragraphs.original: κύριος γάρ ἐστιν τοῦ σαββάτου ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου.
paragraphs.translit: kyrios gar estin tou sabbatou ho hyios tou anthrōpou.

paragraphs.text: And he departed thence, and went into their synagogue:
paragraphs.original: Καὶ μεταβὰς ἐκεῖθεν ἦλθεν εἰς τὴν συναγωγὴν αὐτῶν·
paragraphs.translit: Kai metabas ekeithen ēlthen eis tēn synagōgēn autōn·

paragraphs.text: and behold, a man having a withered hand. And they asked him, saying, Is it lawful to heal on the sabbath day? that they might accuse him.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἰδοὺ ἄνθρωπος χεῖρα ἔχων ξηράν. καὶ ἐπηρώτησαν αὐτὸν λέγοντες· Εἰ ἔξεστι τοῖς σάββασιν θεραπεύειν; ἵνα κατηγορήσωσιν αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: kai idou anthrōpos cheira echōn xēran. kai epērōtēsan auton legontes· Ei exesti tois sabbasin therapeuein; hina katēgorēsōsin autou.

paragraphs.text: And he said unto them, What man shall there be of you, that shall have one sheep, and if this fall into a pit on the sabbath day, will he not lay hold on it, and lift it out?
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Τίς ἔσται ἐξ ὑμῶν ἄνθρωπος ὃς ἕξει πρόβατον ἕν, καὶ ἐὰν ἐμπέσῃ τοῦτο τοῖς σάββασιν εἰς βόθυνον, οὐχὶ κρατήσει αὐτὸ καὶ ἐγερεῖ;
paragraphs.translit: ho de eipen autois· Tis estai ex hymōn anthrōpos hos hexei probaton hen, kai ean empesē touto tois sabbasin eis bothynon, ouchi kratēsei auto kai egerei;

paragraphs.text: How much then is a man of more value than a sheep! Wherefore it is lawful to do good on the sabbath day.
paragraphs.original: πόσῳ οὖν διαφέρει ἄνθρωπος προβάτου. ὥστε ἔξεστιν τοῖς σάββασιν καλῶς ποιεῖν.
paragraphs.translit: posō oun diapherei anthrōpos probatou. hōste exestin tois sabbasin kalōs poiein.

paragraphs.text: Then saith he to the man, Stretch forth thy hand. And he stretched it forth; and it was restored whole, as the other.
paragraphs.original: τότε λέγει τῷ ἀνθρώπῳ· Ἔκτεινόν σου τὴν χεῖρα· καὶ ἐξέτεινεν, καὶ ἀπεκατεστάθη ὑγιὴς ὡς ἡ ἄλλη.
paragraphs.translit: tote legei tō anthrōpō· Ekteinon sou tēn cheira· kai exeteinen, kai apekatestathē hygiēs hōs hē allē.

paragraphs.text: But the Pharisees went out, and took counsel against him, how they might destroy him.
paragraphs.original: ἐξελθόντες δὲ οἱ Φαρισαῖοι συμβούλιον ἔλαβον κατʼ αὐτοῦ ὅπως αὐτὸν ἀπολέσωσιν.
paragraphs.translit: exelthontes de hoi Pharisaioi symboulion elabon katʼ autou hopōs auton apolesōsin.

paragraphs.text: And Jesus perceiving [it] withdrew from thence: and many followed him; and he healed them all,
paragraphs.original: Ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς γνοὺς ἀνεχώρησεν ἐκεῖθεν. καὶ ἠκολούθησαν αὐτῷ πολλοί, καὶ ἐθεράπευσεν αὐτοὺς πάντας,
paragraphs.translit: Ho de Iēsous gnous anechōrēsen ekeithen. kai ēkolouthēsan autō polloi, kai etherapeusen autous pantas,

paragraphs.text: and charged them that they should not make him known:
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐπετίμησεν αὐτοῖς ἵνα μὴ φανερὸν αὐτὸν ποιήσωσιν,
paragraphs.translit: kai epetimēsen autois hina mē phaneron auton poiēsōsin,

paragraphs.text: that it might be fulfilled which was spoken through Isaiah the prophet, saying,
paragraphs.original: ἵνα πληρωθῇ τὸ ῥηθὲν διὰ Ἠσαΐου τοῦ προφήτου λέγοντος·
paragraphs.translit: hina plērōthē to rhēthen dia Ēsaiou tou prophētou legontos·

paragraphs.text: Behold, my servant whom I have chosen; My beloved in whom my soul is well pleased: I will put my Spirit upon him, And he shall declare judgment to the Gentiles.
paragraphs.original: Ἰδοὺ ὁ παῖς μου ὃν ᾑρέτισα, ὁ ἀγαπητός μου εἰς ὃν εὐδόκησεν ἡ ψυχή μου· θήσω τὸ πνεῦμά μου ἐπʼ αὐτόν, καὶ κρίσιν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν ἀπαγγελεῖ.
paragraphs.translit: Idou ho pais mou hon hēretisa, ho agapētos mou eis hon eudokēsen hē psychē mou· thēsō to pneuma mou epʼ auton, kai krisin tois ethnesin apangelei.

paragraphs.text: He shall not strive, nor cry aloud; Neither shall any one hear his voice in the streets.
paragraphs.original: οὐκ ἐρίσει οὐδὲ κραυγάσει, οὐδὲ ἀκούσει τις ἐν ταῖς πλατείαις τὴν φωνὴν αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: ouk erisei oude kraugasei, oude akousei tis en tais plateiais tēn phōnēn autou.

paragraphs.text: A bruised reed shall he not break, And smoking flax shall he not quench, Till he send forth judgment unto victory.
paragraphs.original: κάλαμον συντετριμμένον οὐ κατεάξει καὶ λίνον τυφόμενον οὐ σβέσει, ἕως ἂν ἐκβάλῃ εἰς νῖκος τὴν κρίσιν.
paragraphs.translit: kalamon syntetrimmenon ou kateaxei kai linon typhomenon ou sbesei, heōs an ekbalē eis nikos tēn krisin.

paragraphs.text: And in his name shall the Gentiles hope.
paragraphs.original: καὶ τῷ ὀνόματι αὐτοῦ ἔθνη ἐλπιοῦσιν.
paragraphs.translit: kai tō onomati autou ethnē elpiousin.

paragraphs.text: Then was brought unto him one possessed with a demon, blind and dumb: and he healed him, insomuch that the dumb man spake and saw.
paragraphs.original: Τότε προσηνέχθη αὐτῷ δαιμονιζόμενος τυφλὸς καὶ κωφός· καὶ ἐθεράπευσεν αὐτόν, ὥστε τὸν κωφὸν λαλεῖν καὶ βλέπειν.
paragraphs.translit: Tote prosēnechthē autō daimonizomenos typhlos kai kōphos· kai etherapeusen auton, hōste ton kōphon lalein kai blepein.

paragraphs.text: And all the multitudes were amazed, and said, Can this be the son of David?
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐξίσταντο πάντες οἱ ὄχλοι καὶ ἔλεγον· Μήτι οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ υἱὸς Δαυίδ;
paragraphs.translit: kai existanto pantes hoi ochloi kai elegon· Mēti houtos estin ho hyios Dauid;

paragraphs.text: But when the Pharisees heard it, they said, This man doth not cast out demons, but by Beelzebub the prince of the demons.
paragraphs.original: οἱ δὲ Φαρισαῖοι ἀκούσαντες εἶπον· Οὗτος οὐκ ἐκβάλλει τὰ δαιμόνια εἰ μὴ ἐν τῷ Βεελζεβοὺλ ἄρχοντι τῶν δαιμονίων.
paragraphs.translit: hoi de Pharisaioi akousantes eipon· Houtos ouk ekballei ta daimonia ei mē en tō Beelzeboul archonti tōn daimoniōn.

paragraphs.text: And knowing their thoughts he said unto them, Every kingdom divided against itself is brought to desolation; and every city or house divided against itself shall not stand:
paragraphs.original: εἰδὼς δὲ τὰς ἐνθυμήσεις αὐτῶν εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Πᾶσα βασιλεία μερισθεῖσα καθʼ ἑαυτῆς ἐρημοῦται, καὶ πᾶσα πόλις ἢ οἰκία μερισθεῖσα καθʼ ἑαυτῆς οὐ σταθήσεται.
paragraphs.translit: eidōs de tas enthymēseis autōn eipen autois· Pasa basileia meristheisa kathʼ heautēs erēmoutai, kai pasa polis ē oikia meristheisa kathʼ heautēs ou stathēsetai.

paragraphs.text: and if Satan casteth out Satan, he is divided against himself; how then shall his kingdom stand?
paragraphs.original: καὶ εἰ ὁ Σατανᾶς τὸν Σατανᾶν ἐκβάλλει, ἐφʼ ἑαυτὸν ἐμερίσθη· πῶς οὖν σταθήσεται ἡ βασιλεία αὐτοῦ;
paragraphs.translit: kai ei ho Satanas ton Satanan ekballei, ephʼ heauton emeristhē· pōs oun stathēsetai hē basileia autou;

paragraphs.text: And if I by Beelzebub cast out demons, by whom do your sons cast them out? therefore shall they be your judges.
paragraphs.original: καὶ εἰ ἐγὼ ἐν Βεελζεβοὺλ ἐκβάλλω τὰ δαιμόνια, οἱ υἱοὶ ὑμῶν ἐν τίνι ἐκβάλλουσιν; διὰ τοῦτο αὐτοὶ κριταὶ ἔσονται ὑμῶν.
paragraphs.translit: kai ei egō en Beelzeboul ekballō ta daimonia, hoi hyioi hymōn en tini ekballousin; dia touto autoi kritai esontai hymōn.

paragraphs.text: But if I by the Spirit of God cast out demons, then is the kingdom of God come upon you.
paragraphs.original: εἰ δὲ ἐν πνεύματι θεοῦ ἐγὼ ἐκβάλλω τὰ δαιμόνια, ἄρα ἔφθασεν ἐφʼ ὑμᾶς ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ θεοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: ei de en pneumati theou egō ekballō ta daimonia, ara ephthasen ephʼ hymas hē basileia tou theou.

paragraphs.text: Or how can one enter into the house of the strong [man,] and spoil his goods, except he first bind the strong [man]? and then he will spoil his house.
paragraphs.original: ἢ πῶς δύναταί τις εἰσελθεῖν εἰς τὴν οἰκίαν τοῦ ἰσχυροῦ καὶ τὰ σκεύη αὐτοῦ ἁρπάσαι, ἐὰν μὴ πρῶτον δήσῃ τὸν ἰσχυρόν; καὶ τότε τὴν οἰκίαν αὐτοῦ διαρπάσει.
paragraphs.translit: ē pōs dynatai tis eiselthein eis tēn oikian tou ischyrou kai ta skeuē autou harpasai, ean mē prōton dēsē ton ischyron; kai tote tēn oikian autou diarpasei.

paragraphs.text: He that is not with me is against me, and he that gathereth not with me scattereth.
paragraphs.original: ὁ μὴ ὢν μετʼ ἐμοῦ κατʼ ἐμοῦ ἐστιν, καὶ ὁ μὴ συνάγων μετʼ ἐμοῦ σκορπίζει.
paragraphs.translit: ho mē ōn metʼ emou katʼ emou estin, kai ho mē synagōn metʼ emou skorpizei.

paragraphs.text: Therefore I say unto you, Every sin and blasphemy shall be forgiven unto men; but the blasphemy against the Spirit shall not be forgiven.
paragraphs.original: διὰ τοῦτο λέγω ὑμῖν, πᾶσα ἁμαρτία καὶ βλασφημία ἀφεθήσεται τοῖς ἀνθρώποις, ἡ δὲ τοῦ πνεύματος βλασφημία οὐκ ἀφεθήσεται.
paragraphs.translit: dia touto legō hymin, pasa hamartia kai blasphēmia aphethēsetai tois anthrōpois, hē de tou pneumatos blasphēmia ouk aphethēsetai.

paragraphs.text: And whosoever shall speak a word against the Son of man, it shall be forgiven him; but whosoever shall speak against the Holy Spirit, it shall not be forgiven him, neither in this world, nor in that which is to come.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ὃς ἐὰν εἴπῃ λόγον κατὰ τοῦ υἱοῦ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου, ἀφεθήσεται αὐτῷ· ὃς δʼ ἂν εἴπῃ κατὰ τοῦ πνεύματος τοῦ ἁγίου, οὐκ ἀφεθήσεται αὐτῷ οὔτε ἐν τούτῳ τῷ αἰῶνι οὔτε ἐν τῷ μέλλοντι.
paragraphs.translit: kai hos ean eipē logon kata tou hyiou tou anthrōpou, aphethēsetai autō· hos dʼ an eipē kata tou pneumatos tou hagiou, ouk aphethēsetai autō oute en toutō tō aiōni oute en tō mellonti.

paragraphs.text: Either make the tree good, and its fruit good; or make the tree corrupt, and its fruit corrupt: for the tree is known by its fruit.
paragraphs.original: Ἢ ποιήσατε τὸ δένδρον καλὸν καὶ τὸν καρπὸν αὐτοῦ καλόν, ἢ ποιήσατε τὸ δένδρον σαπρὸν καὶ τὸν καρπὸν αὐτοῦ σαπρόν· ἐκ γὰρ τοῦ καρποῦ τὸ δένδρον γινώσκεται.
paragraphs.translit: Ē poiēsate to dendron kalon kai ton karpon autou kalon, ē poiēsate to dendron sapron kai ton karpon autou sapron· ek gar tou karpou to dendron ginōsketai.

paragraphs.text: Ye offspring of vipers, how can ye, being evil, speak good things? for out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaketh.
paragraphs.original: γεννήματα ἐχιδνῶν, πῶς δύνασθε ἀγαθὰ λαλεῖν πονηροὶ ὄντες; ἐκ γὰρ τοῦ περισσεύματος τῆς καρδίας τὸ στόμα λαλεῖ.
paragraphs.translit: gennēmata echidnōn, pōs dynasthe agatha lalein ponēroi ontes; ek gar tou perisseumatos tēs kardias to stoma lalei.

paragraphs.text: The good man out of his good treasure bringeth forth good things: and the evil man out of his evil treasure bringeth forth evil things.
paragraphs.original: ὁ ἀγαθὸς ἄνθρωπος ἐκ τοῦ ἀγαθοῦ θησαυροῦ ἐκβάλλει ἀγαθά, καὶ ὁ πονηρὸς ἄνθρωπος ἐκ τοῦ πονηροῦ θησαυροῦ ἐκβάλλει πονηρά.
paragraphs.translit: ho agathos anthrōpos ek tou agathou thēsaurou ekballei agatha, kai ho ponēros anthrōpos ek tou ponērou thēsaurou ekballei ponēra.

paragraphs.text: And I say unto you, that every idle word that men shall speak, they shall give account thereof in the day of judgment.
paragraphs.original: λέγω δὲ ὑμῖν ὅτι πᾶν ῥῆμα ἀργὸν ὃ λαλήσουσιν οἱ ἄνθρωποι, ἀποδώσουσιν περὶ αὐτοῦ λόγον ἐν ἡμέρᾳ κρίσεως·
paragraphs.translit: legō de hymin hoti pan rhēma argon ho lalēsousin hoi anthrōpoi, apodōsousin peri autou logon en hēmera kriseōs·

paragraphs.text: For by thy words thou shalt be justified, and by thy words thou shalt be condemned.
paragraphs.original: ἐκ γὰρ τῶν λόγων σου δικαιωθήσῃ, καὶ ἐκ τῶν λόγων σου καταδικασθήσῃ.
paragraphs.translit: ek gar tōn logōn sou dikaiōthēsē, kai ek tōn logōn sou katadikasthēsē.

paragraphs.text: Then certain of the scribes and Pharisees answered him, saying, Teacher, we would see a sign from thee.
paragraphs.original: Τότε ἀπεκρίθησαν αὐτῷ τινες τῶν γραμματέων καὶ Φαρισαίων λέγοντες· Διδάσκαλε, θέλομεν ἀπὸ σοῦ σημεῖον ἰδεῖν.
paragraphs.translit: Tote apekrithēsan autō tines tōn grammateōn kai Pharisaiōn legontes· Didaskale, thelomen apo sou sēmeion idein.

paragraphs.text: But he answered and said unto them, An evil and adulterous generation seeketh after a sign; and there shall no sign be given it but the sign of Jonah the prophet:
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Γενεὰ πονηρὰ καὶ μοιχαλὶς σημεῖον ἐπιζητεῖ, καὶ σημεῖον οὐ δοθήσεται αὐτῇ εἰ μὴ τὸ σημεῖον Ἰωνᾶ τοῦ προφήτου.
paragraphs.translit: ho de apokritheis eipen autois· Genea ponēra kai moichalis sēmeion epizētei, kai sēmeion ou dothēsetai autē ei mē to sēmeion Iōna tou prophētou.

paragraphs.text: for as Jonah was three days and three nights in the belly of the whale; so shall the Son of man be three days and three nights in the heart of the earth.
paragraphs.original: ὥσπερ γὰρ ἦν Ἰωνᾶς ἐν τῇ κοιλίᾳ τοῦ κήτους τρεῖς ἡμέρας καὶ τρεῖς νύκτας, οὕτως ἔσται ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ τῆς γῆς τρεῖς ἡμέρας καὶ τρεῖς νύκτας.
paragraphs.translit: hōsper gar ēn Iōnas en tē koilia tou kētous treis hēmeras kai treis nyktas, houtōs estai ho hyios tou anthrōpou en tē kardia tēs gēs treis hēmeras kai treis nyktas.

paragraphs.text: The men of Nineveh shall stand up in the judgment with this generation, and shall condemn it: for they repented at the preaching of Jonah; and behold, a greater than Jonah is here.
paragraphs.original: ἄνδρες Νινευῖται ἀναστήσονται ἐν τῇ κρίσει μετὰ τῆς γενεᾶς ταύτης καὶ κατακρινοῦσιν αὐτήν· ὅτι μετενόησαν εἰς τὸ κήρυγμα Ἰωνᾶ, καὶ ἰδοὺ πλεῖον Ἰωνᾶ ὧδε.
paragraphs.translit: andres Nineuitai anastēsontai en tē krisei meta tēs geneas tautēs kai katakrinousin autēn· hoti metenoēsan eis to kērygma Iōna, kai idou pleion Iōna hōde.

paragraphs.text: The queen of the south shall rise up in the judgment with this generation, and shall condemn it: for she came from the ends of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon; and behold, a greater than Solomon is here.
paragraphs.original: βασίλισσα νότου ἐγερθήσεται ἐν τῇ κρίσει μετὰ τῆς γενεᾶς ταύτης καὶ κατακρινεῖ αὐτήν· ὅτι ἦλθεν ἐκ τῶν περάτων τῆς γῆς ἀκοῦσαι τὴν σοφίαν Σολομῶνος, καὶ ἰδοὺ πλεῖον Σολομῶνος ὧδε.
paragraphs.translit: basilissa notou egerthēsetai en tē krisei meta tēs geneas tautēs kai katakrinei autēn· hoti ēlthen ek tōn peratōn tēs gēs akousai tēn sophian Solomōnos, kai idou pleion Solomōnos hōde.

paragraphs.text: But the unclean spirit, when he is gone out of the man, passeth through waterless places, seeking rest, and findeth it not.
paragraphs.original: Ὅταν δὲ τὸ ἀκάθαρτον πνεῦμα ἐξέλθῃ ἀπὸ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου, διέρχεται διʼ ἀνύδρων τόπων ζητοῦν ἀνάπαυσιν, καὶ οὐχ εὑρίσκει.
paragraphs.translit: Hotan de to akatharton pneuma exelthē apo tou anthrōpou, dierchetai diʼ anydrōn topōn zētoun anapausin, kai ouch heuriskei.

paragraphs.text: Then he saith, I will return into my house whence I came out; and when he is come, he findeth it empty, swept, and garnished.
paragraphs.original: τότε λέγει· Εἰς τὸν οἶκόν μου ἐπιστρέψω ὅθεν ἐξῆλθον· καὶ ἐλθὸν εὑρίσκει σχολάζοντα σεσαρωμένον καὶ κεκοσμημένον.
paragraphs.translit: tote legei· Eis ton oikon mou epistrepsō hothen exēlthon· kai elthon heuriskei scholazonta sesarōmenon kai kekosmēmenon.

paragraphs.text: Then goeth he, and taketh with himself seven other spirits more evil than himself, and they enter in and dwell there: and the last state of that man becometh worse than the first. Even so shall it be also unto this evil generation.
paragraphs.original: τότε πορεύεται καὶ παραλαμβάνει μεθʼ ἑαυτοῦ ἑπτὰ ἕτερα πνεύματα πονηρότερα ἑαυτοῦ, καὶ εἰσελθόντα κατοικεῖ ἐκεῖ· καὶ γίνεται τὰ ἔσχατα τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐκείνου χείρονα τῶν πρώτων. οὕτως ἔσται καὶ τῇ γενεᾷ ταύτῃ τῇ πονηρᾷ.
paragraphs.translit: tote poreuetai kai paralambanei methʼ heautou hepta hetera pneumata ponērotera heautou, kai eiselthonta katoikei ekei· kai ginetai ta eschata tou anthrōpou ekeinou cheirona tōn prōtōn. houtōs estai kai tē genea tautē tē ponēra.

paragraphs.text: While he was yet speaking to the multitudes, behold, his mother and his brethren stood without, seeking to speak to him.
paragraphs.original: Ἔτι δὲ αὐτοῦ λαλοῦντος τοῖς ὄχλοις ἰδοὺ ἡ μήτηρ καὶ οἱ ἀδελφοὶ αὐτοῦ εἱστήκεισαν ἔξω ζητοῦντες αὐτῷ λαλῆσαι.
paragraphs.translit: Eti de autou lalountos tois ochlois idou hē mētēr kai hoi adelphoi autou heistēkeisan exō zētountes autō lalēsai.

paragraphs.text: And one said unto him, Behold, thy mother and thy brethren stand without, seeking to speak to thee.
paragraphs.original: εἶπεν δέ τις αὐτῷ· Ἰδοὺ ἡ μήτηρ σου καὶ οἱ ἀδελφοί σου ἔξω ἑστήκασιν, ζητοῦντές σοι λαλῆσαι.
paragraphs.translit: eipen de tis autō· Idou hē mētēr sou kai hoi adelphoi sou exō hestēkasin, zētountes soi lalēsai.

paragraphs.text: But he answered and said unto him that told him, Who is my mother? and who are my brethren?
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν τῷ λέγοντι αὐτῷ· Τίς ἐστιν ἡ μήτηρ μου, καὶ τίνες εἰσὶν οἱ ἀδελφοί μου;
paragraphs.translit: ho de apokritheis eipen tō legonti autō· Tis estin hē mētēr mou, kai tines eisin hoi adelphoi mou;

paragraphs.text: And he stretched forth his hand towards his disciples, and said, Behold, my mother and my brethren!
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐκτείνας τὴν χεῖρα αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ εἶπεν· Ἰδοὺ ἡ μήτηρ μου καὶ οἱ ἀδελφοί μου·
paragraphs.translit: kai ekteinas tēn cheira autou epi tous mathētas autou eipen· Idou hē mētēr mou kai hoi adelphoi mou·

paragraphs.text: For whosoever shall do the will of my Father who is in heaven, he is my brother, and sister, and mother.
paragraphs.original: ὅστις γὰρ ἂν ποιήσῃ τὸ θέλημα τοῦ πατρός μου τοῦ ἐν οὐρανοῖς, αὐτός μου ἀδελφὸς καὶ ἀδελφὴ καὶ μήτηρ ἐστίν.
paragraphs.translit: hostis gar an poiēsē to thelēma tou patros mou tou en ouranois, autos mou adelphos kai adelphē kai mētēr estin.
